To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Credit Default Swap spreads are significantly and positively related with the equity capitalization, the financial leverage and the reserve for loan loss, while they are negatively related with the book-to-market ratio.

the Credit Default Swap spread can be estimated by a log linear function of four explanatory variables determined by the accounting data, the market quotes, the official ratings, and the macroeconomic variables.
our model is able to explain 70% of the variation in the CDS spreads and that the explanatory variables have the expected sign.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an econometric model for estimating the Credit Default Swap spread for banks.
the estimation of Credit Default Swaps for European banks.
the estimation of Credit Default Swap spreads using accounting data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model has the potential to become a valuable tool for risk managers and analysts in the banking sector.
accounting data and market quotes are the main determinants of Credit Default Swap spreads.
our results confirm the existence of a significant relation between Credit Default Swap spreads, accounting data and market variables.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our model is able to explain the default risk of a bank by means of its own financial structure, its equity composition and its accounting data.

we provide evidence that accounting data are useful to explain the Credit Default Swap spreads and that the Credit Default Swap spread can be estimated using accounting data, official ratings, market quotes and macroeconomic indicators.

the proposed model is useful for the evaluation of the default risk of banks, the estimation of their theoretical Credit Default Swaps spread and the identification of those banks that have the highest default risk.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a significant portion of Credit Default Swap spreads can be explained by accounting data and official ratings, and that the model is able to capture the impact of the financial crisis and the subsequent sovereign debt crisis on European banks' credit default risk.

in the European context the Credit Default Swap spread can be estimated using accounting data, the market quotes, the official ratings of banks and macroeconomic variables, and the model has a good predictive power.
the model is a useful tool for the estimation of banks' credit spreads, especially in the current European context where the official ratings of banks do not reflect their true credit risk.
